title: Why Did Canyon Do This?

takeaways.text: A 45 mm Panaracer GravelKing X1 fitted the fork with no problem, but at the rear it rubbed the drive-side chainstay, so 45 mm could not be run front and rear.
He attributes the 42 mm limit to Canyon supporting a front derailleur and large chainrings; he still calls it a fantastic bike otherwise.
With a 45 mm front and 40 mm rear tire on a 100 km rough ride, the front felt much more controlled and comfortable while the narrower rear was faster on smooth surfaces but less comfortable.
The proprietary seatpost and stem rule out a suspension seatpost, leaving tires as the main comfort lever.

disclosure: How the bike was supplied is not stated; the tires are named as unsponsored. The Grail grade and build tested are not stated, so the frame layup may differ from the CF 7.
summary: A tire-clearance test on the 2024-generation Canyon Grail CF platform rated for 42 mm, with a mixed front/rear tire workaround.
